claims.text: reporting-requirements.md: a report query turns many rows into a few figures about a period, such as revenue per day; placing an order reads and writes a few rows of one order.
capacity-plan.md at stage-4 sends every write and every read to the primary PostgreSQL; db-replica is used only in the lab.

multi-shop-design-review.md records as open, with owner product owner and backend developer: how a report across all shops reads a shop that has its own database (ADR 0026), since one query cannot join two databases.
Since stage-3, payments and refunds live in donhang_payments and orders in donhang. ADR 0026 decides, though stage-4 does not build it, that a shop that moves keeps its orders in its own database.
PostgreSQL: a client connection accesses only the one database named in its connection request; an ordinary query cannot read tables of another database on the same server.

revenue-by-customer.sql lines 5-14 LEFT JOIN payments in the same database as orders; it runs only because the old payments table in donhang is not dropped: ADR 0008 drops it after accounting checks it against donhang_payments.

claims.text: Readers: a shop's staff see only their shop; Đơn Hàng's team sees every shop, including shops with their own database.

Scenarios BC-1..BC-5: revenue, orders, refunds per day with as-of time, at most 2 hours old (assumed); best sellers over a date range, same age; all shops, none missing; a yearly report at peak takes no primary connection; shop A staff see no other shop's figure.
A day is defined in Vietnam time (assumed) because orders-by-day.sql shows orders on different days in UTC and Vietnam time; its second query lists those, placed in the early morning Vietnam time.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/reporting-requirements.md @ stage-4 lines 37-38; db/queries/orders-by-day.sql @ stage-4 lines 4-19

claims.text: Estimate: 50,000 orders/normal day (capacity-plan.md), kept 2 years (assumed): ~36 M orders; a one-year report reads ~18 M orders with line rows, tens of millions of rows; 5 years ~90 M; a report holds a connection thousands of times longer (assumed s vs ms).
Assumptions table: product owner with a few shops confirms '2 hours old is enough'; accounting confirms 'day in Vietnam time'; product owner with accounting confirms 2-year retention.

Ranked drivers: (1) reports never take capacity ordering needs (BC-4); (2) each shop sees only its own figures (BC-5); (3) reports across shops include shops in their own databases (BC-3). The file states no reason for the order; BC-1, BC-2 are not ranked.

Figures up to two hours old with an as-of time leave room to compute away from ordering; up-to-the-second figures tie reports to source tables at busy hours and are worth it only when a late figure has a measurable cost; reusing the SQL file is wrong for revenue.
UTC days are one fixed rule but count early-morning Vietnam orders on the previous day; recording 'Vietnam time, assumed' with accounting as confirmer keeps the choice cheap to revisit.

Choices: a different day-closing hour changes the reporting day before design; a live-figure demand needs a measurable loss and a new scenario; 5-year retention changes the stored total the design is sized from, so redo the estimate first.
Trust in report figures comes from showing how old they are (as-of time) rather than from being up to the second, when staff read the day's results.
PostgreSQL row-level security adds a condition to the queries a role runs on a table (superusers, BYPASSRLS roles and normally the table owner bypass it).
In revenue-by-customer.sql, customers LEFT JOIN orders LEFT JOIN payments keeps every customer even when no order or payment matches.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs 7.2.1.1 Joined Tables (LEFT OUTER JOIN)

claims.text: A PostgreSQL server accepts at most a configured number of concurrent connections (max_connections), so a connection held by a report is unavailable to orders meanwhile.
Vietnam time runs ahead of UTC: orders placed in the early morning Vietnam time are still on the previous day in UTC.
When ordering is how shops earn money, a slow report costs less than a slow order, which fits BC-4 ranking first; unranked scenarios must still be met, ranking only settles conflicts.
